title: Presentation / Briefing Slides (Ch 7)
source: Defence Forces Service Writing Manual 2024 (JP-04), Chapter 7
notes: Rules for PowerPoint briefing and presentation decks. Slide text is checked against the same core conventions (fonts, underlining, dates, abbreviations, security markings) while Word-only layout rules (margins, page numbers, footnotes) are deliberately excluded — a slide deck is not a page-formatted document.

rules.title: Opening title slide
rules.description: The deck should open with a title slide carrying the subject, date and security grading so the audience knows what and when the briefing covers.
rules.notes: Human review: confirm slide 1 is a title slide showing the subject, date and security grading before the briefing content begins.

rules.title: Approved font family
rules.description: Slide text must use an approved service font (Times New Roman or Arial); decorative fonts weaken the professional standard.

check.where: All text in shapes on every slide

autofix.description: Sets the deck text to the first approved font.

rules.title: No underlining for emphasis
rules.description: Underlining must not be used for emphasis in typed text, including slide text; emphasis is shown by bold or capital letters.

autofix.description: Removes underlining from all slide text.

rules.title: Security grading on every slide
rules.description: Each slide must carry the security classification (e.g. RESTRICTED) so the grading travels with the material.

rules.title: Dates in day-month-year order
rules.description: Dates on slides must be written in day-month-year order (e.g. 13 Aug 26) with no leading noughts and no comma.

rules.title: Abbreviations explained on first use
rules.description: Abbreviations must be written in full the first time they are used, followed by the abbreviation in brackets, on the slide where they first appear.

rules.title: Confine slides to essentials
rules.description: Briefings must be confined to essentials; commanders are busy and must not be bothered with unnecessary detail (avoid dense, full-sentence slides).
rules.notes: Human review: scan each slide for dense blocks of full-sentence text and split or reduce to key points.

rules.title: Aim stated at the outset
rules.description: The briefing should open by stating its aim, in line with the requirement and terms of reference (Step One — The Scope).
rules.notes: Human review: confirm the aim of the briefing is stated early, e.g. 'The aim of this briefing is to ...'.

rules.title: Legible, consistent text sizes
rules.description: Body text must be large enough to be read from the back of the room and sizes should be consistent across slides.
rules.notes: Human review: check font sizes are legible at the back of the room and consistent slide-to-slide.

rules.title: Slide numbers
rules.description: Slides should be numbered so the audience and the officer can refer to a specific slide during discussion and decision points.
rules.notes: Human review: confirm slide numbers are visible on each slide (e.g. 'Slide 3 of 12').
